sourceOrder.performanceTask: predict, question and summarise a text

developmental.approach: Conceptual foundations, guided investigations and foundational computing

requirements: Two or three measurable objectives derived from the performance task; MOE mapping recorded as PROPOSED, never claimed
At least two distinct, named misconceptions, each taught against and diagnosed by a block
Hints in every guided scene; no hints or worked steps in independent scenes
Choice items with three or more plausible options, or richer interactions
No system, policy or answer-policy text in learner-visible fields; no generator prefixes; UTF-8 text with no mojibake
Specific learner actions in every scene
Guided practice, independent work, extension and reflection, in that order
An authentic Liberian situation that needs the concept, not a name swap
Formative only: no grade, mastery or assessment keys in the learner projection

objectives.statement: Make a plausible prediction from a story detail and revise it when new information appears.
Ask a question that can guide further reading and distinguish an unanswered question from a known fact.
Write a short summary that connects the main problem, response and result without adding unsupported details.

misconceptions.description: A plausible prediction is reported as something the story has already established.
misconceptions.response: Name the detail that makes the idea plausible, use might or may, and change the prediction if later evidence conflicts.

misconceptions.description: A summary lists incidental details or invents an outcome instead of connecting the central problem, response and result.
misconceptions.response: Keep the problem, the action taken and the result supported by the story; remove details that do not explain that connection.

answerGuidance.prediction: Accept any plausible tentative prediction grounded in the opening. A later mismatch is not itself an error. The pupil must distinguish an explicit detail from a forecast and identify a question the opening does not answer.
answerGuidance.guided: Select the blurred names and the risk of visitors taking an unidentified plant. The useful unresolved question asks whether the labels remain clear after another shower. Carrying the tin is a known action, not the reason clear names matter.
answerGuidance.independent: The sheltered label stayed clearer in the two comparisons described; no universal guarantee follows. The best summary links blurred labels, the comparison and sheltered storage after the results.
answerGuidance.writing: Example, 42 words: Rain made the school garden labels hard to read before a seedling exchange. Massa's class compared an open label with a sheltered one. After two showers, the sheltered label stayed clearer. They stored spare labels under shelter and planned to keep checking. Accept other faithful wording. Check a connected problem/response/result, no invented events, and a relevant unanswered question. The model answer belongs to reviewer guidance, not to the independent task.
answerGuidance.revision: A valid revision identifies the pupil's own earlier wording, changes or sharpens it and cites the text detail that justifies the change. An extension might propose a heavier shower causing a sheltered label to blur, which would require changing or retesting the plan. Do not require pupils to report an activity they did not do.

segments.activity: Read the opening only and record a prediction/question
Model a clue, prediction and unresolved question
Reveal the ending and compare predictions
Write a summary and a useful question
Revise a claim with textual evidence

teacherGuide.support: Read each paragraph aloud without revealing the ending early. Offer separate problem/action/result boxes and let a pupil dictate while directing the wording. Ask which sentence supports each claim; do not supply the independent answer.
teacherGuide.extension: Compare two plausible predictions from the opening, explain why later evidence supports one more strongly and propose a new observation that could change the recommendation.
teacherGuide.block90Proposal: After the 45-minute core, compare two different faithful summaries for 15 minutes, write a short alternative ending and trace which predictions it changes for 15 minutes, then peer-review and revise for 15 minutes. This is a proposed extension, not measured timing.
teacherGuide.assessment: No governed assessment or official score is supplied. All questions are ungraded practice; future independent assessment remains a separate request.
teacherGuide.offline: Print the opening and ending on separate sheets. Keep the ending covered until after prediction. Read passages and options aloud as needed; pupils select evidence or dictate responses on paper. No audio asset or device voice is promised.
teacherGuide.retention: Request a different short narrative after at least seven days, with the same predict/question/summarize strategy. No event is scheduled here.

references.title: Original LiberiaLearn narrative and reading activities
references.use: All story text, choices, explanations and prompts are original. The class, comparison and observations are fictional; no real pupil data or measured investigation is represented.
